notes: Static question bank + generator spec. The AI uses 'bank' as reference and backup; if it cannot generate a good question it falls back along generation.fallback_chain. Asked-history is stored per user in Google Drive, NOT in this file. Math duel answers are computed by the app. Assumptions to check: mode names (math_duel, weekly_boss, matrix) and their behaviour match your app; edit 'modes' if not.

context_fields.r_multiple_min: number (rule helper: matches if r_multiple >= value)
context_fields.r_multiple_max: number (rule helper: matches if r_multiple <= value)
context_fields.trade_number_min: integer (rule helper: matches if trade_number_today >= value)

selection_rules: 1. Pick the mode from where the user is in the app (journal, chart view, math duel, weekly boss, matrix).
2. Keep bank questions whose mode matches (or 'any') and whose 'when' matches the context. Empty 'when' always matches.
3. Remove questions asked in the last 'cooldown_trades' trades (asked-history lives in the user's Google Drive data).
4. Multiply weight by 0.5 for each time a question was asked in the last 30 days.
5. Weighted-random pick, with at least 'min_categories' categories and at least 2 different question types per session.
6. With probability 'wildcard_chance', swap one pick for a wildcard.
7. Run the fallback_chain in 'generation'. Always have a question to show.
8. Save asked ids, generated-question hashes and dates to asked-history.

chart_display.purpose: Questions shown while a chart (live or replay) is on screen. Prefer interactive types.
chart_display.tone: short and visual, one action per question

math_duel.purpose: Timed trading-maths rounds (position size, R, expectancy, P&L). Answers are computed by the APP, not the AI.
math_duel.difficulty_ramp: start easy, move up a level after 3 correct in a row, down after 2 wrong
math_duel.tone: fast, no explanations until the round ends

weekly_boss.purpose: Once a week the user fights their biggest recurring mistake of the week, in 3 phases: scout (see the pattern), weak_point (find the trigger), final_blow (commit to one rule). Optional reward phase.
weekly_boss.boss_selection: Pick boss_type from the week's data (most R lost or most frequent). If data is unclear, ask boss-90 and use the answer. If still unclear, rotate through boss types not used in the last 3 weeks.
weekly_boss.tone: game-like and serious about the lesson

matrix.purpose: Place trades in a grid and read the pattern.

question_types.how_to_ask: Free text. Ask for specific details, not general feelings.
Ask for a 1-10 score, then ask what caused the missing points.
Give 3-5 plausible options including an honest-but-uncomfortable one.
A direct claim about the trade. Follow with one 'why' line.
Ask the user to order factors by responsibility for the result.
Sentence with blanks the user completes. Good for rules and plans.
Ask for a single word, then ask why.
Ask for a percentage before and after the outcome, then compare.
Change one variable (size, stop, entry, wait) and ask what would change.
Ask the user to argue against their own trade.
Ask how a risk manager, a friend, or future-you would see the trade.
Put two trades side by side and ask what differs.
Ask the user to find the mistake and write it as a rule.
Ask the user to mark a zone, point or candle on the chart.
Show several marked levels and ask which one mattered.
Pause the replay and ask what happens next.
Ask the user to place trades into a grid.
Give numbers, ask for one calculated value. App computes the right answer.

perspective: a coach who has never seen your result
you on your best trading day
level_kind: the liquidity you expected to be taken

math_duel.contract_spec_note: MNQ: $2 per index point, tick size 0.25 points = $0.50 per tick per contract. Verify against the contract spec in the app and change here if different.
math_duel.evaluation: APP evaluates 'answer' with its own safe expression evaluator after sampling params. The AI must never compute or reveal answers.

items.text: MNQ long {contracts} contract(s): entry {entry}, exit {exit}. What is the P&L in $?
MNQ short {contracts} contract(s): entry {entry}, exit {exit}. What is the P&L in $?
Price moves {points} points. How many ticks is that on MNQ?
You risk {risk} points on a trade and make {reward} points. What is the R multiple?
Your stop is {stop_pts} points away and you can risk ${risk_usd}. How many MNQ contracts can you trade (round down)?
With a {rr}:1 reward-to-risk ratio, what win rate (%) do you need to break even?
Win rate {wr}%, average win {avg_win}R, average loss 1R. What is your expectancy in R per trade?
Your account is down {dd}%. What percent gain do you need to get back to even?
Your win probability is {wr}%. What is the probability (%) of {n} losses in a row?
Gross profit ${gp}, gross loss ${gl}. What is the profit factor?
You take half off at +{r1}R and let the rest hit +{r2}R. What is the blended R on the full position?
Daily loss limit is ${limit}. You have lost ${lost}. With a {stop_pts}-point stop, how many 1-contract MNQ losses can you take before hitting the limit (round down)?
You risk {risk_pct}% per trade on a ${acct} account with a {stop_pts}-point stop. How many MNQ contracts (round down)?
A trade makes ${pnl} with {contracts} contract(s) and a {stop_pts}-point stop. What was the R multiple?

generation.formula: question = mode x focus x type x lens x time_ref x perspective, then fill with the trade's real data.

anti_repeat.rule: Never reuse the same key within the last 8 sessions of the same mode. Never reuse the exact same wording within 30 days.
anti_repeat.if_exhausted: Change the type first, then the lens, then the perspective, then the focus.

must_include: At least one concrete detail from the trade (time, level, session, R, size, or emotion tag).
One clear thing to answer, not two questions in one.
Wording that is different from the last 5 questions asked.
must_avoid: Questions answerable without looking at the trade.
Asking about data the user has not provided (do not invent trade details).
precision_rules: If trade data is missing a field, ask about the field instead of guessing it.
Match the mode: chart questions must name one action on the chart; math duel questions must be numeric and unambiguous; weekly boss questions must reference the week, not a single trade.
Keep questions under 30 words unless the type needs options.
fallback_chain: 1. Rewrite a matching bank question with the trade's details.
2. Fill a template with slot pools, choosing slots that match the trade.
3. Free-generate using the formula and rules above, using the bank as style reference.
4. Use a bank question unchanged (lowest-used one matching 'when').

ai_prompts.rewrite: You are a trading coach. Trade: {trade_json}. Base questions: {questions_json}. Rewrite each as a short, specific question using real details from this trade. Keep what each question tests. No praise. Return JSON: [{"id":"...","question":"..."}].
ai_prompts.generate_new: You are a trading coach. Mode: {mode}. Trade/context: {trade_json}. Recently asked: {recent_questions}. Generate {n} NEW questions using focus x type x lens from the generation rules. Use these example questions as style reference: {bank_samples}. Do not repeat or lightly reword recent questions. Return JSON: [{"type":"...","question":"...","options":[]}].
ai_prompts.chart_display: A chart is on screen with these marks: {chart_context}. Ask {n} questions, each requiring ONE action on the chart (mark, choose, predict). Return JSON with a 'chart_action' field for each.
ai_prompts.math_duel: Do NOT compute answers. Only add a one-line flavour intro for the round if asked. The app samples numbers and checks answers itself.
ai_prompts.weekly_boss: Week data: {week_json}. Boss type: {boss_type}. Write a short boss intro (2 sentences, game-like) naming the actual pattern from the data. Then ask the phase questions for the current phase: {phase}. Reference the week, not one trade.
ai_prompts.matrix: Grid: {layout}. Trades placed: {placements_json}. Ask {n} questions about the pattern in the grid, naming the actual cells and counts.
